reasoning_traces.think:
The core operator is a recursive Bayesian filter that blends a static prior (XGBoost) with dynamic momentum updates. The momentum M_x(t) is a martingale difference sequence adjusted by exponential decay, which ensures that older information loses influence as the match progresses. The final blend P^{final}_{live}(t) = P^{pre}_{win}(p_1|e^{pre})·(1 + s_x/S)·M_x(t)·w(t) + (1 - w(t))·P^{pre}_{win}(p_1|e^{pre}) acts as a shrinkage estimator, pulling the live probability toward the pre-match baseline when uncertainty is high (large remaining points). This structure guarantees that P^{final}_{live}(t) lies within [0,1]. The shielding mechanism exploits the fact that many user queries can be answered exactly from a pre-built knowledge base, thus avoiding the stochasticity of LLM sampling. However, the reliance on tennis-specific rules (e.g., sets won scaling) creates a brittle coupling to the sport; transferring this to football would require redefining 'sets' as quarters/halves and recalibrating the set-booster.
